title: Check a dependency's presence with require.resolve, not a literal node_modules path
body:
Do not check `join(pluginRoot, 'node_modules', '<pkg>', 'package.json')` with fs.access -- it only exists for a dev checkout with its own local node_modules. Use `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('<pkg>/package.json')` instead: it walks up through node_modules the same way the real `import` elsewhere in the codebase will resolve at runtime, so it succeeds under hoisting and still throws the same way (MODULE_NOT_FOUND) when genuinely absent.

Why: Found and fixed 2026-09-19 in scripts/install-codex.mjs's planCodexInstall during docs/plans/2026-09-19-harness-native-install-plan.md's own done-when verification: `npm pack` + install into a scratch project (deliberately not `npm link`, which would have hidden this by preserving a direct node_modules layout) reproduced a real ENOENT that never showed up in the dev-checkout test suite.

evidence.summary: planCodexInstall's dependency-presence check, fixed from fs.access on a literal path to require.resolve.
fix: resolve the SDK dependency check through node_modules hoisting -- includes the require.resolve replacement and the commit message documenting the reproduction steps.
Anchored delivery: keywords validated against this memory's own text and a generic-request corpus before proposing.

v1.trigger: Writing or reviewing an installer/CLI script that verifies one of its own npm dependencies is present before doing work, for a package meant to be run both from a dev checkout (own local node_modules) and as an installed dependency elsewhere (npx / npm install, where npm hoists deps to the consumer's top-level node_modules).
